memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua built on Mount Ebal an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded the Israelites. He built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses — an altar of uncut stones, on which no iron tool had been used. On it they offered to the Lord burnt offerings and sacrificed fellowship offerings. There, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua wrote on stones a copy of the law of Moses. — Josh 8:30-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the battles, Joshua does something that might surprise us. He does not rush on to the next conquest. Instead, he stops to worship. He builds an altar on Mount Ebal, offers sacrifices, and writes out God's law on stones. In the middle of a military campaign, worship and God's word take centre stage. This tells us where Joshua's true priorities lay. Victory in battle was never the ultimate goal; knowing and honouring God was.

Notice the altar was built exactly "according to what is written," of uncut stones, just as God had commanded through Moses (Ex 20:25). Joshua was careful to worship God in God's way, not his own. True worship follows God's instructions rather than human invention. And the stones inscribed with the law show how central Scripture was — God's people were to have His word before their eyes.

There is deep wisdom for us here. After seasons of hard work or success, our instinct is often to press on to the next thing. But Joshua models the priority of pausing to worship and to soak in God's word. We are not meant to live from achievement to achievement, but to keep returning to the altar and to Scripture, remembering who our God is and living in fellowship with Him.

The altar with its burnt offerings and fellowship offerings points us forward to Christ. Every sacrifice on that altar anticipated the one perfect sacrifice of Jesus, who offered Himself once for all (Heb 10:10). Because of His finished work, we now draw near to God not through animal sacrifices but through Christ, offering ourselves in grateful worship and living in true fellowship with our God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you pause to worship and return to God's word, or rush from one thing to the next?
2. Are you careful to worship God in the way He has shown, not merely as you prefer?
3. How does Christ's once-for-all sacrifice shape the way you draw near to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me make worship and Your word my true priority, not just achievement. Thank You for Christ, the perfect sacrifice, through whom I draw near to You. Amen.
